To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The incidence of breast cancer in the United States is increasing; 2) Breast cancer is more common in white women, and in women with a family history of breast cancer; and 3) The incidence of early‐stage breast cancer is increasing, and this is due to increased mammography screening.

(1) The overall survival of patients with pT1NOM0 breast carcinoma at 10 years is 80%, (2) The overall survival at 10 years for patients with a positive margin is only 50%, and (3) The overall survival for patients with a negative margin at 10 years exceeds 90%.
The 5‐year survival rate for patients with pT1NOM0 breast cancer is 95%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long‐term outcome and the late mortality of patients with pT1NOM0 breast carcinoma.
the development of new, more effective, and safer anticancer drugs.
the development of a mathematical model that can be used to predict the long‐term survival of patients with pT1NOM0 breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prognosis of patients with pT1N1M0 breast cancer is not as good as that of patients with pN0M0 disease.

the prognosis of patients with pT1N1 breast cancer is similar to that of pT1N2 patients and both are significantly poorer than pT1NOM patients, but the prognosis of pT2N0 patients is similar to that for pT1N3 patients.
the long term outcome for patients with pT1N1M0 breast carcinoma is better than that for patients with pN0M0 disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an increased risk of death from pT1 breast cancer compared with women without breast cancer.
we are still not able to predict the outcome for patients with pT1NOM0 breast carcinoma, even when using the most advanced prognostic factors.
the majority of patients with pT1NOM0 disease will be alive at 15 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the long term outcome for patients with early stage breast cancer is excellent, even for patients who have a recurrence.
we need to do more to help patients with breast cancer who are at high risk for late mortality.
the majority of women with pT1N1M0 breast cancer are cured with breast‐conserving treatment.
